The publication-disabled simulated-Actions build-core run and independent native-local build-core run reproduced the package, resolver metadata, build logs, and both ABI artifacts byte for byte. Both profiles satisfy the exact fail-closed 2048 16-source C-only compile, ordered-link, source, native-version, dependency, and diagnostic proof.

The pristine source is commit c90437d3c3913999624deca3fb55ecfa632b72c4, tree 5b8bcab69dc90185f10356b5780bf9d827684474, with no submodules. The proof binds upstream's native leading-space short hash to all 16 C compile commands and the exact C link invocation. The selected source is eight commits newer than the shipped 86e02d3 baseline and includes software-framebuffer and continue-after-2048 behavior changes, so the candidate requires fresh runtime validation.

Both builds clone the exact source over the network; no offline source bundle or network-disabled rebuild is proven. The portable toolchain archives and loaded image identities are locked, but cached images retain dockerfile_linkage=unverified-local-cache as an explicit provenance limitation.

The root source license is the Unlicense/Public Domain dedication, while selected libretro-common files retain their own permissive notices. Resolver metadata reports Public Domain. Any public distribution or release remains a human legal and policy gate even though the local bytes reproduce.

Resolver metadata reports supports_no_game=true and savestate=true with serialized save states, matching the exported serialization APIs. It reports libretro_saves=false while the source exposes nonzero RETRO_MEMORY_SAVE_RAM; metadata was preserved unchanged, and SaveRAM behavior, software-framebuffer rendering, controls, reset, save-state round trips, expected silence/no-audio initialization behavior, frontend integration, and sustained performance remain target-runtime gates.

ARM64 requires GLIBC_2.17 and records the AArch64 loader, libc, and libm. ARMHF is EABI5 hard-float, reaches GLIBC_2.7, and records libc and libm. The software-only artifacts bind only to ra64-universal-v1 and ra32-a30-v1 and provide no basis for device-specific duplicate builds; all device views remain ineligible pending provider and target-runtime evidence.
